decisions.rationale: Incineroar+Rotom-Wash lead: Intimidate and Fake Out disrupt early, Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump threatens both Tyranitar and Excadrill 2× SE while Levitate blanks Excadrill's Ground moves. Volt Switch enables pivoting. Dragapult (213 Speed) outspeeds even Mega Gengar (max 200) and Shadow Ball OHKOs it; Metagross-Mega brings Bullet Punch priority and SE Psychic Fangs/Meteor Mash against Gengar/Tyranitar. This four covers the expected Gengar+Houndoom lead and the sand backline while retaining late-game cleaning power.

Lead Tyranitar+Gengar to set sand while Gengar-Mega Taunts shut down Corviknight Tailwind and Klefki screens—the two biggest threats to the sand core. Excadrill+Houndoom on bench: Excadrill provides sand-rush offense at 140 Speed, Houndoom covers Metagross-Mega (Flamethrower SE), Corviknight (Flamethrower SE), Incineroar (Flash Fire+Dark resist), and Dragapult (absorbs Fire Blast via Flash Fire, Sucker Punch priority). Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball is SE on Metagross/Dragapult; Shadow Tag traps key targets. Houndoom chosen over Gholdengo (weak to Psychic Fangs/Thunderbolt, no Taunt) and Tauros (Intimidate bounced by Mirror Armor).
decisions.notebook: G3 plan: opponent almost certainly brings Metagross-Mega+Corviknight (both benched G2) plus Dragapult and one support mon. Gengar-Mega Taunt is the only answer to both Klefki screens and Corviknight Tailwind on my team—must lead or early-switch it to prevent speed control. Metagross-Mega Adamant speed 130-162 can outspeed Excadrill's 140 sand speed; in Tailwind (195-243) it outspeeds everything I have. Houndoom at 161 Speed is a near-tie with max-speed Metagross-Mega (162)—expect to lose that speed tie at max investment. Dragapult (178-213) outspeeds Gengar-Mega (165-200); Protect Gengar if Dragapult leads. Flash Fire Houndoom walls Dragapult's Fire Blast and Incineroar's Fire moves; Dark typing resists Darkest Lariat and Shadow Ball. Key KO checks needed turn 1: Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball vs Metagross-Mega, Houndoom Flamethrower vs Corviknight/Metagross-Mega, Excadrill High Horsepower vs Metagross-Mega.

decisions.rationale: Switch Rotom-Wash to Metagross to dodge the expected Helping Hand + Mega Gengar Energy Ball combo that would OHKO Rotom (77.7-110.8% with base Gengar + Helping Hand, likely >100% with Mega). Metagross takes only 14.6-21% from resisted Energy Ball. Fake Out on Tyranitar prevents Rock Slide (though Helping Hand at +5 resolves first). We preserve Rotom-Wash for later and bring in Metagross, who threatens Gengar with a guaranteed OHKO from Psychic Fangs. Turn 2 we can double-target Gengar or pivot based on what the opponent reveals.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Opponent leads Gengar + Tyranitar (Smooth Rock). Turn 1 they likely use Helping Hand + Mega Gengar Energy Ball into our Rotom slot. Gengar-Mega outspeeds our entire team except Dragapult. Tyranitar's Helping Hand (+5) outpaces Fake Out (+3). Metagross Psychic Fangs guarantees OHKO on Gengar. Dragapult Shadow Ball is 85.6-167.4% vs Gengar and Dragapult outspeeds Mega Gengar (213 vs 165-200). Sand setter Tyranitar is the priority target for Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump later. Excadrill (Sand Rush, Focus Sash) and Houndoom (Life Orb, Flash Fire) are the likely back line.

decisions.rationale: Helping Hand (pri +5) resolves before Incineroar Fake Out (pri +3), so Tyranitar safely boosts Gengar-Mega's Energy Ball into 73.9–139.2% range on Rotom-Wash—possible OHKO. Gengar Mega Evolves for Shadow Tag and outspeeds both foes (178 vs 80–112 / 106–138). If Incineroar predicts and uses Darkest Lariat on Gengar (guaranteed OHKO), Gengar still acts first and gets Energy Ball off, trading favorably for Rotom-Wash. Fake Out chip on Tyranitar is only 3.4–5.3%. This is the maximum-pressure turn-1 play that can remove Rotom-Wash and establish Shadow Tag.
decisions.notebook: G3T1: Mega Evolved Gengar, used Helping Hand+Energy Ball on Rotom-Wash. Key facts confirmed: Helping Hand pri+5 beats Fake Out pri+3 so HH is safe vs Fake Out flinch. Incineroar Darkest Lariat is guaranteed OHKO on Gengar/Mega Gengar (119-175%). Gengar-Mega Energy Ball+HH vs Rotom-W = 74-139% (possible OHKO through Sitrus). Rotom-W Hydro Pump vs Gengar = 66-97%. If Gengar survives T1, Shadow Tag locks opponent—prioritize protecting Gengar next turn if Incineroar still has Darkest Lariat. Opponent benched 2 of: Dragapult/Klefki/Corviknight/Metagross-Mega. Excadrill (140 sand speed) and Houndoom (161, Flash Fire) in back for Metagross-Mega/Dragapult matchups.

decisions.rationale: Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball OHKOs Metagross (99.4-138.9%) before Metagross can move. Switching Metagross to Dragapult preserves Metagross and brings in the only mon that outspeeds Gengar-Mega (213 vs 165-200). Dragapult Shadow Ball does 74.9-138.5% to Gengar; Incineroar Darkest Lariat adds 61.1-117%. Dragapult moves before Gengar, so if Shadow Ball KOs, Gengar never attacks. If Dragapult rolls low, Gengar OHKOs Dragapult but Incineroar finishes Gengar. Either way Gengar-Mega is removed at the cost of at most Dragapult, leaving Metagross and Rotom-Wash in reserve.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Opponent leads Gengar-Mega + Tyranitar (Smooth Rock, 8-turn sand). Turn 1 they used Helping Hand + Energy Ball into Metagross (now 65%). Excadrill (Sand Rush, Focus Sash) and Houndoom (Life Orb, Flash Fire) are the likely back line. Dragapult is our only Gengar-Mega outspeed; preserve it if possible. Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump threatens Tyranitar. Metagross Psychic Fangs is a roll to OHKO Gengar-Mega (91-173.3%).

decisions.rationale: Metagross is trapped by Shadow Tag and Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball is a guaranteed OHKO (99.4–138.9%). Protect saves Metagross while Mega Evolving grants Tough Claws for future turns. Incineroar Darkest Lariat into Gengar-Mega deals 61.1–117%, a possible KO; even if it falls short, Mega Metagross can revenge with Tough Claws-boosted Bullet Punch next turn. This preserves both Pokémon and applies maximum pressure to the opponent's fast special attacker.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Opponent leads Gengar-Mega + Tyranitar (Smooth Rock). Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag traps our team. Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball OHKOs Metagross. Incineroar Darkest Lariat is our best Gengar-Mega damage (61-117%). Metagross must Protect to survive. Excadrill (Sand Rush, Sash) and Houndoom (Life Orb, Flash Fire) are the likely back line. Dragapult outspeeds Gengar-Mega; preserve it as a late-game answer.

decisions.rationale: Gengar Protects to dodge guaranteed OHKOs from Incineroar Darkest Lariat and Metagross Psychic Fangs, preserving Shadow Tag which is critical for keeping the opponent locked in. Tyranitar Crunches Metagross (SE 2x, 27-48% chip) for insurance. Next turn Gengar Shadow Ball guarantees KO on Metagross from any HP while Shadow Tag remains active, forcing opponent's 4th Pokémon in while Incineroar stays trapped. If opponent predicts and targets Tyranitar instead, TTar likely survives at low HP and Gengar still cleans up Metagross next turn.
decisions.notebook: G3T2: Gengar Shadow Ball GUARANTEED KO on Metagross at 64% (77-141%). Metagross Psychic Fangs GUARANTEED KO on Gengar (120-171%). Incineroar Darkest Lariat GUARANTEED OHKO on Gengar (119-175%). Metagross Bullet Punch does 28-42% to Gengar (not KO). Gengar (200) outspeeds Incineroar (80-112). Plan: Protect Gengar T2 to preserve Shadow Tag, chip Metagross with TTar Crunch, then KO Metagross T3 with Shadow Ball while Shadow Tag keeps Incineroar trapped. Opponent's 4th Pokémon forced in after Metagross faints. Key: never let Gengar die while Shadow Tag is needed — opponent has Dragapult (178-213) that outspeeds all my remaining mons if freed.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Shadow Tag prevents switching. Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball is a guaranteed OHKO on Metagross-Mega (85.4-118.5%). Protect (+4 priority) resolves before Shadow Ball; even at ~33% success after consecutive use, it is the only path to keep Metagross-Mega alive. Incineroar Darkest Lariat into Gengar-Mega (61.1-117%) threatens a KO and is our best damage. If Protect fails, we lose Metagross-Mega but still get the Darkest Lariat chip; if Protect succeeds, we preserve a 2v2 or 2v1 position. The double-Bullet-Punch line guarantees the Gengar trade but sacrifices the 33% chance of a dominant board state, which is worth the variance in a decisive game 3.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Opponent leads Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag) + Tyranitar (Smooth Rock). Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball OHKOs Metagross-Mega. Incineroar Darkest Lariat is our best Gengar-Mega damage (61-117%). Metagross-Mega Protect is the only survival tool despite reduced success. Dragapult outspeeds Gengar-Mega and is preserved as a late-game answer. Excadrill (Sand Rush, Sash) and Houndoom (Life Orb, Flash Fire) are the likely back line.

decisions.rationale: Switch Gengar to Excadrill to preserve Shadow Tag user at 88% — opponent most likely targets Gengar (their primary threat), wasting both attacks when it switches out. Tyranitar Crunch chips Metagross from 64% to ~20-38%. Next turn Excadrill at 280 Speed (Sand Rush) outspeeds everything and KOs chipped Metagross with High Horsepower (58.8-100.6%). Even worst case (opponent predicts switch, Metagross Meteor Mash possibly KOs Tyranitar at 81-114%), I'm 3v2 with Gengar preserved. This is strictly better than trading Gengar for Metagross, which leaves 3v2 with no Shadow Tag and no speed control answer to potential Dragapult.
decisions.notebook: G3T3 plan: Switch Gengar→Excadrill (preserve Shadow Tag), TTar Crunch chips Metagross to 20-38%. T4: Excadrill (280 Spe in sand) KOs chipped Metagross with High Horsepower (guaranteed KO from 20-38%). Excadrill resists Metagross Steel STAB (0.5x), neutral to Darkest Lariat (44-64%). TTar Meteor Mash from Metagross is possible KO (81-114% vs 97% HP) if opponent predicts switch. Key: keep Gengar alive for Shadow Tag re-trap; Excadrill Sand Rush outspeeds Dragapult (178-213). Opponent 4th mon is one of Dragapult/Klefki/Corviknight (Rotom-Wash already revealed).

decisions.rationale: Excadrill under Sand Rush outspeeds both my active Pokémon and OHKOs either with High Horsepower. Switching Incineroar to Rotom-Wash gives me a Levitate pivot immune to Ground, while Metagross-Mega's Bullet Punch (+1 priority) breaks Excadrill's Focus Sash before it moves. Even if Excadrill KOs Metagross with High Horsepower targeting that slot, I break Sash and preserve Incineroar for later Intimidate cycling. Rotom-Wash then threatens Excadrill with Hydro Pump next turn and can Volt Switch to regain momentum. Dragapult remains in the back as a Gengar-Mega answer.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Opponent leads Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag) + Tyranitar (Smooth Rock). Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball OHKOs Metagross-Mega. Incineroar Darkest Lariat is our best Gengar-Mega damage (61-117%). Metagross-Mega Protect is the only survival tool despite reduced success. Dragapult outspeeds Gengar-Mega and is preserved as a late-game answer. Excadrill (Sand Rush, Sash) and Houndoom (Life Orb, Flash Fire) are the likely back line. Rotom-Wash Levitate is key to blanking Excadrill's Ground moves.

decisions.rationale: Bring Incineroar for the Intimidate re-apply and fresh Fake Out. Intimidate drops Tyranitar to -2 and Excadrill to -1, neutering their physical pressure. Rotom-Wash passes so the move can be decided with full turn-5 information. Dragapult stays benched as the Gengar-Mega answer.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Opponent leads Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag) + Tyranitar (Smooth Rock). Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball OHKOs Metagross-Mega. Incineroar Darkest Lariat is our best Gengar-Mega damage (61-117%). Dragapult outspeeds Gengar-Mega and is preserved as a late-game answer. Excadrill (Sand Rush, Sash) and Houndoom (Life Orb, Flash Fire) are the likely back line; Gholdengo and Tauros-Aqua also possible. Rotom-Wash Levitate blanks Excadrill's Ground moves. Incineroar's Intimidate re-applies on switch-in, stacking with prior drops. Excadrill High Horsepower threatens Incineroar even at -1 (55-78%), so Fake Out control on Excadrill is critical.

decisions.rationale: Helping Hand guarantees Excadrill's High Horsepower KOs Metagross-Mega (87.7-148.4% with HH vs 64% HP, guaranteed KO). Without HH, High Horsepower alone is only 58.8-100.6% — not a guaranteed KO from 64%. Excadrill at 280 Speed moves before both foes, so Metagross is removed before it can act (Meteor Mash was a possible KO on Tyranitar at 81-114%). Incineroar's Flare Blitz is a guaranteed KO on Excadrill at 50% HP regardless, so Excadrill is likely traded — but that's a favorable swap (broken-sash Excadrill at 50% for Metagross-Mega at 64%). Tyranitar stays at 97% and I retain Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag) and Houndoom (100%) in back for the 3v3 endgame.
decisions.notebook: G3T4: HH+HHP into Metagross = guaranteed KO. Excadrill likely falls to Flare Blitz (guaranteed KO at 50%). After trade: TTar 97% + Gengar-Mega 88% + Houndoom 100% vs Incineroar 82% + Rotom-Wash 100% + unknown 4th. Plan: bring Gengar-Mega next to Shadow Tag trap; Gengar Shadow Ball hits Incineroar neutral, Rotom-Wash neutral. Houndoom resists Incineroar Dark/Fire and Metagross Steel (if it somehow survived). TTar Rock Slide chips Incineroar (SE 2x). Opponent 4th mon is one of Dragapult/Klefki/Corviknight. Excadrill has no good answer for Rotom-Wash (Levitate blocks HHP, all other moves NVE). Key: preserve Gengar for Shadow Tag endgame control.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out on Excadrill neutralises the fastest, most threatening spread attacker (Sand Rush Rock Slide). Hydro Pump into Tyranitar deals 41.5–75.4%, pressuring the Sand setter and exploiting the free turn created by the flinch. Even if Excadrill Protects, Tyranitar still eats the Hydro Pump and its -2 Rock Slide is manageable; double Protect wastes both their Protects. Volt Switch is too weak (13.5–24%) and pivoting Dragapult into Rock/Dark moves is unsafe.

Switch Tyranitar to Gengar-Mega to activate Shadow Tag, trapping both foes before they can switch to their unknown 4th mon. Excadrill Protects — opponent most likely targets Excadrill (26% HP, easy KO), wasting both their moves. Next turn pivot Excadrill to Houndoom for free switch-in while Gengar attacks. Endgame: Gengar+Houndoom outspeed both trapped foes, Houndoom resists Incineroar's STABs, Gengar Energy Ball hits Rotom-Wash SE. Switching the 97% HP Tyranitar is far safer than switching the 26% Excadrill to bring in Gengar.
decisions.notebook: G3: Shadow Tag trapping is the win condition — must get Gengar-Mega on field before opponent can switch to 4th mon. Gengar 200 Spe + Houndoom 161 Spe both outspeed Rotom-Wash (106-138) and Incineroar (80-112). Houndoom resists Incineroar Fire/Dark (0.5x) and Flash Fire absorbs Fire. Gengar Energy Ball SE on Rotom-Wash (2x Grass vs Water). Opponent 4th mon unknown: Dragapult/Klefki/Corviknight — Klefki Prankster TWave and Dragapult outspeeding Gengar are biggest threats, making Shadow Tag trapping critical. TTar at -2 Atk is dead weight offensively; sand persists 4 turns without TTar on field. Excadrill at 26% with sash gone is expendable — best used as Protect pivot for safe Houndoom entry.

decisions.rationale: Gengar at 2% almost certainly Protects; Excadrill's High Horsepower has a roll to OHKO Incineroar (54.5–78.2% into 76%). Incineroar Protect blocks that KO. Rotom-Wash Will-O-Wisp burns Excadrill through Protect, permanently neutering its Attack (already -1) regardless of Gengar's action. If Gengar unexpectedly attacks, Rotom risks the Energy Ball KO but Gengar remains at 2% and can be revenged by Dragapult. Next turn Gengar's Protect success is reduced, letting us finish it.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Opponent leads Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag) + Tyranitar (Smooth Rock). Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball OHKOs Metagross-Mega. Incineroar Darkest Lariat is our best Gengar-Mega damage (61-117%). Dragapult outspeeds Gengar-Mega and is preserved as a late-game answer. Excadrill (Sand Rush, Sash) and Houndoom (Life Orb, Flash Fire) are the likely back line; Gholdengo and Tauros-Aqua also possible. Rotom-Wash Levitate blanks Excadrill's Ground moves. Incineroar's Intimidate re-applies on switch-in, stacking with prior drops. Excadrill High Horsepower threatens Incineroar even at -1 (55-78%), so Fake Out control on Excadrill is critical. Will-O-Wisp on Excadrill permanently cripples it. Gengar-Mega Protect usage tracked: used turn 2 only; consecutive Protect reduction applies next use.

decisions.rationale: Gengar dies to sandstorm at 3% regardless; both my Pokémon outspeed both foes. Energy Ball is SE on Rotom (61-114% of max HP, ~49% KO chance from 88%) and High Horsepower is SE on Incineroar (52-93% of max HP, ~41% KO chance from 76%). Going for double KO potential is far superior to switching, since Rotom Hydro Pump OHKOs Houndoom (112-167%), making any switch-in extremely risky. Even if no KO, both foes are heavily chipped and I keep Houndoom (100%) + Tyranitar (97%) fresh on bench for cleanup.
decisions.notebook: G3: Houndoom is OHKO'd by Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump (2x Water vs Fire, 112-167% of max HP) — never switch Houndoom into a slot Rotom might target. Tyranitar tanks Hydro Pump (36-55% of max HP, survives). Gengar-Mega at 3% dies to sandstorm (Ghost/Poison not immune). Energy Ball on Rotom: 61-114% of max HP (possible KO from 88%). Excadrill High Horsepower on Incineroar at -1 Atk: 52-93% of max HP (possible KO from 76%). Opponent 4th mon unknown (Dragapult/Klefki/Corviknight); Shadow Tag ends when Gengar leaves field. Sandstorm has 3 turns left; TTar sandstream can refresh if brought back in. Houndoom resists Incineroar Dark/Fire (0.5x each) and Flash Fire absorbs Fire; best late-game cleaner if kept safe from Water moves.

decisions.rationale: Gengar fainted; bring in Tyranitar (97% HP) which resists Incineroar's Flare Blitz (0.5x) and Darkest Lariat (0.5x) and survives Rotom's Hydro Pump (36-55%). Houndoom must stay in back — it's OHKO'd by Hydro Pump (112-167%) and is our best late-game cleaner once Rotom is removed. Excadrill is at 20% burned with -1 Atk and can only Pass; it will likely faint soon, after which Houndoom enters with Tyranitar as a safe pivot. Never forfeit with two healthy mons remaining.
decisions.notebook: G3 endgame plan: Tyranitar (97%, -2 Atk from 2 Intimidates) resists Incineroar's Fire/Dark (0.5x each) and tanks Rotom Hydro Pump (36-55%). Houndoom (100%, Life Orb, Timid) is OHKO'd by Rotom Hydro Pump — must not enter until Rotom is eliminated. Excadrill (20%, brn, -1 Atk, Focus Sash consumed) is nearly dead; burn ticks ~12 HP/turn. Opponent 4th mon unknown (Dragapult/Klefki/Corviknight). Path to win: chip/force out Rotom-Wash (29%), then bring Houndoom to clean up Incineroar (resists Dark/Fire 0.5x, Flash Fire absorbs Fire). Tyranitar Rock Slide at -2 Atk is weak but can provide chip; Helping Hand can boost Houndoom late.

decisions.rationale: Rotom-Wash Protect (priority +4) blocks all incoming attacks, crucially stopping Tyranitar Crunch which would otherwise OHKO Rotom-Wash (35-50.3%). Excadrill moves before Incineroar but its Rock Slide only does 10.9-15.3% to Incineroar. Incineroar Flare Blitz then guarantees the KO on Excadrill (77.4-149.2%), removing the fastest threat. Rotom-Wash is preserved at 30% to threaten Tyranitar with Hydro Pump (41.5-75.4%) next turn. Worst case: Tyranitar also Rock Slides Incineroar for 44.6-63.4%, total 55.5-78.7% — Incineroar survives except on extreme dual high rolls. This line preserves both Pokémon and secures a KO.
decisions.notebook: Game 3: Opponent's last unrevealed is one of Houndoom/Gholdengo/Tauros-Aqua. Dragapult outspeeds all three and has super-effective coverage (Thunderbolt for Tauros-Aqua, Shadow Ball/Fire Blast for Gholdengo, Thunderbolt for Houndoom). Preserve Dragapult as endgame cleaner. Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump is our best Tyranitar damage; keep it alive. Incineroar's Intimidate has been applied twice to Tyranitar (-2 Atk). Excadrill burned and -1 Atk, Focus Sash still intact but irrelevant at 20% HP. Sandstorm has 2 turns remaining.

decisions.rationale: Focus-fire Rotom-Wash (29%): Excadrill Rock Slide (5.7-11.2% chip, moves first at 280 Speed) + Tyranitar Crunch (28.7-52.8%) = 34.4% minimum combined, guaranteed KO from 29% if both connect. Excadrill is dying from burn anyway so extracting value now is essential. Rock Slide also chips Incineroar (10.4-18.2%). If Rotom Protects, we still damage Incineroar and can retry Crunch next turn. Once Rotom falls, Houndoom can safely enter to clean up Incineroar with Flash Fire absorbing Fire and resisting Dark.
decisions.notebook: G3 win path: eliminate Rotom-Wash first (Houndoom is OHKO'd by Rotom Hydro Pump, cannot enter while Rotom lives). Once Rotom is gone, bring Houndoom to clean up Incineroar (resists Dark/Fire 0.5x, Flash Fire absorbs Fire). Tyranitar at -2 Atk from Intimidates is weak but Crunch is neutral on Rotom and Rock Slide is SE on Incineroar for chip. Opponent 4th mon unknown (Dragapult/Klefki/Corviknight) — Houndoom Dark Pulse hits Dragapult/Klefki SE; watch for Klefki Prankster TWave and Corviknight Tailwind.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Incineroar cannot use Fake Out (not first turn out) so Houndoom is free to move. Houndoom Dark Pulse OHKOs Rotom before it can act. The only play that preserves any winning chance: Rotom uses Protect (~33% consecutive success) while Incineroar switches to Dragapult (switches resolve before moves). If Protect succeeds, Turn 9 presents Rotom+Dragapult vs both foes with Sandstorm gone; Dragapult can Protect to bait Houndoom's Dark Pulse while Rotom Hydro Pumps Houndoom for a possible OHKO. If Protect fails, Dragapult takes only Rock Slide and we lose Rotom, but the alternative plays all lead to certain loss.
decisions.notebook: Game 3, endgame: Dragapult is our sole remaining win condition; it outspeeds everything. Houndoom's Dark Pulse threatens OHKO on Dragapult. Rotom Hydro Pump can OHKO Houndoom but Rotom is outsped. Incineroar's Fake Out is unavailable after being in play multiple turns. Tyranitar at -2 Atk.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Houndoom Dark Pulse guarantees the KO on Rotom-Wash at 24% HP (38.2-72% damage) and Houndoom outspeeds Rotom (161 vs 106-138), so Rotom dies before it can Hydro Pump (which would OHKO Houndoom). Tyranitar Rock Slide hits both foes: SE on Incineroar (33.7-63.5%, possible KO at 43% HP) and chips Rotom if it somehow survives. If Rotom Protects (reduced success rate), Rock Slide still punishes Incineroar. This executes the win path: eliminate Rotom this turn, then clean up Incineroar with Houndoom next turn.
decisions.notebook: G3 win path confirmed: Houndoom Dark Pulse guarantees KO on Rotom at 24% (38-72% range), outspeeds 161 vs 138 max. Rotom Hydro Pump OHKOs Houndoom (112-167%) so Rotom must die before acting. Tyranitar Rock Slide at -2 Atk does 33.7-63.5% to Incineroar (possible KO at 43%). After Rotom falls, Houndoom walls Incineroar (resists Dark 0.5x, Flash Fire immune to Fire). Opponent 4th mon still unknown (Dragapult/Klefki/Corviknight); Houndoom Dark Pulse SE on Dragapult/Klefki. Watch Klefki Prankster TWave and Corviknight Tailwind for speed control.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out fails (Incineroar not first turn out). Dragapult cannot OHKO either foe and both foes OHKO it back (Houndoom Dark Pulse 99-147%, Tyranitar Crunch 59-85%). Houndoom's Sucker Punch also threatens 44-68% before Dragapult moves. Dragapult Protect (+4) blocks all incoming damage; Sucker Punch fails against Protect. Incineroar Darkest Lariat chips Houndoom (18-37%) for a sliver of future hope. This preserves Dragapult one turn while dealing chip to the faster, Dark-Pulse-carrying threat.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 endgame: Dragapult is our sole remaining win condition, outspeeds both foes but cannot OHKO either. Houndoom's Dark Pulse and Tyranitar's Crunch both OHKO Dragapult. Houndoom also carries Sucker Punch. Incineroar's Fake Out unavailable after not being first turn out. Position is heavily lost; Protect + chip is the only line that buys an extra turn.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Dragapult for guaranteed elimination: Houndoom Dark Pulse is a guaranteed KO (77-149% on 52% HP), with Tyranitar Crunch as backup (38-71%, ~50% KO chance). Neither foe can KO either of my Pokémon this turn. If Incineroar Fake Outs Houndoom, Crunch still chips Dragapult to near-zero, enabling Sucker Punch priority KO next turn. If Dragapult Protects, both miss but next turn Incineroar can't Fake Out and Dark Pulse guarantees the KO. Once Dragapult falls, 2v1 vs Incineroar at 43% is an easy sweep.
decisions.notebook: G3 endgame: Houndoom Dark Pulse guaranteed KO on Dragapult at 52%. Tyranitar Crunch 38-71% on Dragapult (backup). Neither foe can KO my mons in one hit. Sucker Punch priority +1 finishes low-HP Dragapult if Houndoom flinches. After Dragapult falls, 2v1 vs Incineroar 43% is won. Houndoom walls Incineroar (Flash Fire immune to Fire, resists Dark 0.5x).

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Dragapult's Protect has a 1/3 chance to succeed after last turn's successful Protect. If it works, Dragapult survives the double dark-move targeting and Incineroar chips Houndoom with Darkest Lariat (18-37%). Next turn we can double Houndoom for a guaranteed KO (Thunderbolt + Darkest Lariat min 46% > max remaining 39%), leaving Incineroar vs -1 Tyranitar. If Protect fails, Dragapult faints but Houndoom is still chipped, giving Incineroar a slim chance to Protect-stall and pick off a weakened Houndoom. No other line keeps Dragapult alive; attacking with Dragapult guarantees its death and leaves Incineroar alone with less cumulative damage on the foes.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 endgame: Dragapult is our sole remaining win condition, outspeeds both foes but cannot OHKO either. Houndoom's Dark Pulse and Tyranitar's Crunch both OHKO Dragapult. Houndoom also carries Sucker Punch. Incineroar's Fake Out unavailable after not being first turn out. Position is heavily lost; Protect + chip is the only line that buys an extra turn. Dragapult's Protect is at 1/3 success rate after turn 9 success. If Dragapult survives turn 10 via Protect, turn 11 double-target Houndoom for KO, then Incineroar must 1v1 Tyranitar.

decisions.rationale: Houndoom Dark Pulse is a guaranteed KO on Dragapult at 52% (77.4–148.5%). Tyranitar Rock Slide hits both foes and chips Incineroar for 24–42% (SE, spread-adjusted), setting up the 2v1 endgame. If Dragapult Protects again (reduced success rate), Rock Slide still lands on Incineroar. Dragapult is faster but cannot KO Houndoom in one hit, so Dark Pulse resolves regardless. After Dragapult falls, Houndoom walls Incineroar (Flash Fire immunity + Dark resist) and Tyranitar's Rock Slide pressure closes it out.
decisions.notebook: G3 endgame confirmed: Houndoom Dark Pulse guaranteed KO on Dragapult at 52%. Tyranitar Rock Slide does 24-42% to Incineroar (SE, spread, at -1). After Dragapult falls, 2v1 vs Incineroar is won: Houndoom walls Incineroar completely (Flash Fire immune to Fire, resists Dark 0.5x), Tyranitar Rock Slide SE on Incineroar. Incineroar Fake Out is spent (used twice, no longer first-turn eligible). Dragapult Protect success rate reduced after consecutive use.

decisions.rationale: Position is lost with no winning line. Dragapult Thunderbolt guarantees KO on Houndoom, but Tyranitar Crunch OHKOs Dragapult in return. Incineroar at 11% cannot 1v1 Tyranitar from 96%: Flare Blitz does 14-24% and Darkest Lariat 10-17%, neither a 2HKO range before Tyranitar KOs back. Dragapult Protect is only 33% and even if it works, the follow-up turn fails to secure the game. Forfeit is the correct competitive decision.
decisions.notebook: Game 3 endgame analysis: with Incineroar at very low HP and Dragapult unable to OHKO Tyranitar, the position is unwinnable even if Houndoom is removed. Dragapult's Protect at 1/3 offers no viable path because Tyranitar alone cleans up both remaining Pokémon.

reflections.summary: The game and series were lost primarily due to a critical piloting error on turn 4, where Mega Metagross was left in against Excadrill and got OHKOed by a Helping Hand-boosted High Horsepower, costing us our Mega early. A subsequent failed Protect on Rotom-Wash (turn 8) led to its KO, leaving an unwinnable 2v2 endgame against Tyranitar and Houndoom. The team composition was reasonable, but these misplays, combined with the opponent's effective use of sand offense and Helping Hand, sealed the loss. Between-game adjustments are unknown, but the brought four were appropriate; the loss stemmed from execution rather than preparation.
reflections.adjustment: In a future series, bring Klefki over Dragapult to set dual screens, which blunts the opponent's special attackers (Mega Gengar, Houndoom) and helps Mega Metagross survive Ground moves. Lead Incineroar + Klefki to safely set screens and cycle Intimidate, then pivot to Rotom-Wash or Metagross as needed. Alternatively, if keeping Dragapult, adjust the game plan to always Protect or switch Metagross when Excadrill is on the field, and avoid consecutive Protects on Rotom-Wash.
reflections.notebook: Opponent tendencies: Leads Tyranitar + Mega Gengar frequently; uses Helping Hand on Tyranitar to secure KOs. Key threats: Excadrill under sand with Helping Hand OHKOs Mega Metagross; Houndoom cleans up weakened special attackers. Our counterplay: Intimidate cycling is effective but must be paired with Protect discipline. Rotom-Wash is valuable for Excadrill but vulnerable to Energy Ball from Gengar. Dragapult's speed is useful but lacks immediate OHKO power on Tyranitar. Future prep: prioritize Klefki for screens, or ensure Metagross never faces Excadrill without Protect or a switch. Avoid consecutive Protects on Rotom-Wash to prevent failure.

reflections.summary: Game 3 was won through superior matchup exploitation and a well-executed sand core. Mega Gengar's Energy Ball chunked both Metagross-Mega and Rotom-Wash for super-effective damage, enabling Excadrill to KO Metagross on turn 4 with a Helping Hand-boosted High Horsepower. Houndoom was the series-clinching bring: Flash Fire made it a complete wall to Incineroar's Flare Blitz, and Dark Pulse threatened Dragapult super-effectively while cleanly KOing Rotom-Wash on turn 8. Tyranitar provided sand, Helping Hand support, and consistent Rock Slide chip. The opponent's Dragapult wasted turns 9-10 on consecutive Protects with a heavily reduced success rate, effectively stalling itself out while Incineroar was whittled to 10%. The endgame 2v1 (Tyranitar 97% + Houndoom 22% vs Dragapult 52% + Incineroar 10%) was mathematically won. Series won 2-1.
reflections.adjustment: The Game 3 bring of Mega Gengar / Tyranitar / Excadrill / Houndoom was optimal for this opponent and needs no changes in a future series. Houndoom as the specialist answer to Incineroar + Dragapult was the decisive adjustment. If anything, consider whether Gholdengo offers value as an alternative to Excadrill if the opponent adapts and brings Klefki for screens, but the current four are the default keep.
reflections.notebook: Opponent tends to bring: Mega Metagross, Incineroar, Rotom-Wash, Dragapult; leaves Klefki and Corviknight on bench. Incineroar relies heavily on Darkest Lariat as primary damage; Fake Out used early and spent quickly. Dragapult spams Protect consecutively even at reduced success rate—punish with chip and positioning rather than respecting it. Rotom-Wash Protects at low HP, sometimes consecutively (can fail). Metagross-Mega Protects predictably on turn 2. Opponent's Incineroar runs Chople Berry; Dragapult runs Life Orb. Houndoom is the key tech: Flash Fire walls Incineroar entirely, Dark Pulse KOs Dragapult and Rotom-Wash. Mega Gengar Energy Ball is critical for chunking Metagross and Rotom-Wash. Tyranitar Helping Hand + Excadrill High Horsepower reliably KOes Metagross-Mega. Opponent does not adapt Protect patterns well—consecutive Protect usage is exploitable. Default bring for rematch: Gengar-Mega / Tyranitar / Excadrill / Houndoom.
